price_why: It gives a freelancer a ready-to-build flagship carousel plus three repeatable weekly formats they can pitch to the gym, all using assets the gym already has. That covers weeks of content planning and could go straight into a client deck.
one_line: A researched creative brief that uses cross-niche design patterns (museum labels, chess puzzles, staff picks, railway timetables) to give specific carousel and still formats for an independent bouldering gym's members and nearby first-timers.
strongest: The lead 'label' carousel is fully specified. It has a flat wall photo with a museum-tombstone label as the only type on the cover, the setter's own sentence, a crux crop and a wall-roster slide. It also names clear failure modes (no big grade type, no adjectives, don't write the setter's line for them).
weakest: Much of the length goes on research scaffolding (trend citations, blocked-source lists, reach-unknown design references) that doesn't help make posts. Several formats also depend on setters or staff supplying their own words and schedule dates.
